segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
My name is Marco.
My name is Catherine.
And as you know, we've had a series going about small talk in English.
segments.zh: 如你所知，我们一直在做一个关于英语闲聊的系列。

segments.en: So today's lesson is a part of that series.
segments.zh: 所以今天的课程是该系列的一部分。

segments.en: That's right.
Today we're going to listen to two friends, two girlfriends meeting and they haven't seen each other for a long time.
segments.zh: 今天我们要听两个朋友，两个女朋友见面，他们已经很久没有见面了。

segments.en: So we're just going to see how they quickly have a small conversation.
segments.zh: 所以我们只是要看看他们如何快速进行小对话。

segments.en: Hey Michelle, is that you?
Wow, Grace, long time no see.
Where have you been?
Oh yeah, well, you see I got a promotion so I moved to the new Pudong office last September.
segments.zh: 哦，是的，你看我得到了晋升，所以我去年九月搬到了新的浦东办公室。

segments.en: You did?
Congratulations.
Thanks a lot.
So how are things with you, Michelle?
segments.zh: 那么你的情况如何，米歇尔？

segments.en: Well, same old, same old, you know, nothing much has changed here.
segments.zh: 好吧，老样子，老样子，你知道，这里没有太大的变化。

segments.en: Are you still seeing Chris?
segments.zh: 你还在跟克里斯交往吗？

segments.en: No, actually we split up last month.
segments.zh: 不，实际上我们上个月分手了。

segments.en: Oh dear, I'm sorry to hear that.
segments.zh: 哦，亲爱的，我很遗憾听到这个消息。

segments.en: But I met a really cute guy last night at a networking party.
segments.zh: 不过昨晚在一个社交聚会上，我遇到了一个很帅的男生。

segments.en: So well, let's just wait and see.
Good for you, Michelle.
All right, we're back.
So now let's take a look at some of the language on Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 所以现在让我们来看看语言要点栏目里的一些表达。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
So the first word we have here today, Marco, is the word promotion.
segments.zh: 所以我们今天在这里的第一个词，Marco，是 promotion（晋升）这个词。

segments.en: Grace says, well, you see, I got a promotion so I moved to the new Pudong office.
segments.zh: 格蕾丝说，好吧，你看，我得到了升职，所以我搬到了新的浦东办公室。

segments.en: That's right.
So she got a promotion and a promotion is work related.
segments.zh: 所以她得到了晋升，晋升与工作有关。

segments.en: That means that you got a better position.
segments.zh: 这意味着你得到了一个更好的职位。

segments.en: That's right.
But you didn't change companies.
So in your company, you had a job and you did well in that job.
segments.zh: 所以在你的公司里，你有一份工作，而且你在那份工作中做得很好。

segments.en: And so your boss gave you a better job in the company.
segments.zh: 所以老板在公司里给了你一份更好的工作。

segments.en: And that's a promotion.
That's right.
Okay, so she got a promotion.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以她得到了晋升。

segments.en: Grace, when they were talking about work and now they started talking about their personal life and Grace asked if Michelle is still seeing Chris.
segments.zh: 格蕾丝，当他们谈论工作时，现在他们开始谈论他们的个人生活，格蕾丝问米歇尔是否还在见克里斯。

segments.en: Okay, so the verb here is to see someone, to be seeing someone.
segments.zh: 好吧，这里的动词是 see someone，也就是 be seeing someone（和某人交往）。

segments.en: We're not actually talking about eyes and looking.
segments.zh: 我们实际上不是在谈论眼睛和看。

segments.en: We're talking about dating.
That's right.
So if you're seeing Chris, it means you are dating Chris.
segments.zh: 所以如果你在跟克里斯交往，就意味着你在和克里斯约会。

segments.en: Okay.
So that's an interesting way of describing a relationship.
segments.zh: 所以这是描述关系的有趣方式。

segments.en: So you say, yeah, I'm sorry, I'm seeing someone.
segments.zh: 所以你说，是的，抱歉，我在和别人交往。

segments.en: I can't date you.
I'm seeing someone else.
Or you could ask someone, are you seeing anyone right now?
segments.zh: 或者你可以问某人，你现在在跟谁交往吗？

segments.en: That means are you dating anyone?
segments.zh: 意思是你在和别人约会吗？

segments.en: Do you have a boyfriend basically?
Okay.
And sadly, no, they are not together anymore.
segments.zh: 可悲的是，不，他们不再在一起了。

segments.en: She says, actually, we split up last month.
segments.zh: 她说，实际上，我们上个月分手了。

segments.en: All right.
So this is another relationship term.
segments.zh: 所以这是另一个关系术语。

segments.en: To split up means to break up or to stop dating.
segments.zh: 分手意味着分手或停止约会。

segments.en: To stop seeing each other.
So there are two ways of seeing it, as you said, to split up or to break up.
segments.zh: 所以有两种说法，正如你所说，split up 或 break up。

segments.en: That's right.
So unfortunately, they split up or unfortunately, they broke up.
segments.zh: 所以不幸的是，他们分手了，或者不幸的是，他们分手了。

segments.en: They are no longer seeing each other.
That's right.
Okay.
But she said she had some good news because she met a really cute guy at a networking party.
segments.zh: 但她说她有一些好消息，因为她在一个社交聚会上遇到了一个很帅的男生。

segments.en: What is networking?
All right.
So networking is something that you do, especially in the business world.
segments.zh: 所以 networking 是你做的一件事，尤其是在商业世界里。

segments.en: You go to events, parties, happy hours, and you meet people.
segments.zh: 你去参加活动、聚会、欢乐时光，你会遇到人。

segments.en: You meet strangers and you talk about work and you try to meet as many people as you can.
segments.zh: 你遇到陌生人，谈论工作，你试图结识尽可能多的人。

segments.en: Okay.
So it's not really a social party to actually just go and meet random people.
segments.zh: 因此，真正去和随机的人会面并不是一个真正的社交派对。

segments.en: You're trying to meet people that will be interesting for your business or maybe to get some other ideas.
segments.zh: 你在努力结识对你的业务有帮助的人，或者能给你带来一些新想法的人。

segments.en: It's for a business purpose.
That's right.
So perhaps in your town, you own a small business and your town has decided to have a chamber of commerce networking party.
segments.zh: 所以也许在你的城镇，你拥有一家小企业，而你的城镇决定举办一个商会的社交聚会。

segments.en: So you can meet other small business owners.
segments.zh: 因此，您可以结识其他小企业主。

segments.en: Okay.
Very good.
So that's what we have for language takeaway.
segments.zh: 这就是我们对语言要点的看法。

segments.en: Let's go back and listen to our dialogue for the second time.
segments.zh: 让我们回去第二次听我们的对话。

segments.en: Hey, Michelle.
Is that you?
Wow, Grace.
Long time no see.
Where have you been?
Oh yeah.
Well, you see, I got a promotion so I moved to the new Pudong office last September.
segments.zh: 好吧，你看，我得到了晋升，所以我去年九月搬到了新的浦东办公室。

segments.en: You did?
Congratulations.
Thanks a lot.
So how are things with you, Michelle?
segments.zh: 那么你的情况如何，米歇尔？

segments.en: Well, same old, same old, you know, nothing much has changed here.
segments.zh: 好吧，老样子，老样子，你知道，这里没有太大的变化。

segments.en: Are you still seeing Chris?
segments.zh: 你还在跟克里斯交往吗？

segments.en: No, actually we split up last month.
segments.zh: 不，实际上我们上个月分手了。

segments.en: Oh dear.
I'm sorry to hear that.
segments.zh: 我很遗憾听到这个消息。

segments.en: But I met a really cute guy last night at a networking party.
segments.zh: 不过昨晚在一个社交聚会上，我遇到了一个很帅的男生。

segments.en: So well, let's just wait and see.
Good for you, Michelle.
All right.

segments.zh: 让我们在流利表达里谈谈这些短小、快速但非常有用的闲聊短语。

segments.en: Fluency Builder.
So this first phrase is a phrase that you'll hear a lot when people greet each other but perhaps friends who haven't seen each other in a very long time.
segments.zh: 所以第一个短语是当人们互相问候时经常听到的，尤其是很久没见的朋友之间。

segments.en: We use this phrase, long time no see.
segments.zh: 我们用这句话，好久不见。

segments.en: That's right.
Now, you look at it and it may seem like it's incorrect, right?
segments.zh: 现在，你看看它，它可能看起来不正确，对吧？

segments.en: Because you're missing something.
segments.zh: 因为这句话缺少了一些成分。

segments.en: That's right.
Long time no see.
Who no see?
What long time?
That's right.
But this actually means I haven't seen you in a long time.
segments.zh: 但这实际上意味着我已经很久没有见到你了。

segments.en: That's right.
So the phrase is long time no see.
segments.zh: 所以这个短语是 long time no see。

segments.en: Hey, Michelle, long time no see.
How are you?
That's the way that you use it.
segments.zh: 这就是你使用它的方式。

segments.en: But just take it as a phrase.
segments.zh: 但只是把它当作一个短语。

segments.en: Don't try to analyze it too much.
So hey, Marco, long time no see.
That's right.
Okay.
And well, they're talking and she's like, well, how are you?
segments.zh: 好吧，他们在说话，她就像，嗯，你好吗？

segments.en: And she says, well, you know, same old, same old.
segments.zh: 她说，嗯，你知道，老样子，老样子。

segments.en: All right.
This is another one.
It doesn't look right.
It doesn't look wrong.
But we do say this and twice, same old, same old.
segments.zh: 但我们确实会这么说，而且要说两遍：same old, same old。

segments.en: And this means nothing has changed.
segments.zh: 这意味着没有任何改变。

segments.en: There's nothing really new in my life.
segments.zh: 我的生活中没有什么新鲜事。

segments.en: Right.
The same old things in my life.
Nothing really new or exciting.
segments.zh: 没有什么真正新鲜或令人兴奋的事。

segments.en: Same old.
Exactly.
So I could say, hey, Marco, how's the job going?
segments.zh: 所以我可以说，嘿，Marco，工作进展如何？

segments.en: You know, same old, same old.
All right.
So nothing has changed in his job.
segments.zh: 所以他的工作没有任何改变。

segments.en: He has not gotten a promotion.
That's right.
So now, Michelle was again describing about the guy that she met at the networking party and she said, well, let's just wait and see.
segments.zh: 所以现在，米歇尔再次说起她在社交聚会上遇到的那个男生，她说，好吧，让我们拭目以待。

segments.en: It seems like an incomplete sentence because let's wait and see what.
segments.zh: 这似乎是个不完整的句子，因为 wait and see 后面还有个 what 没说完。

segments.en: All right.
So let's wait and see what?
That's the question, though.
You know, what are we waiting to see?
segments.zh: 你知道，我们还在等什么？

segments.en: Well, she's basically saying we don't know how things will go, but we, you know, we'll have to wait for the future to come before we can make a decision or figure out what's going on.
segments.zh: 好吧，她基本上是在说我们不知道事情会如何发展，但我们，你知道，我们必须等待未来的到来，才能做出决定或弄清楚发生了什么。

segments.en: That's right.
So, for example, Marco, we're at the office and I say, how is that report coming along?
segments.zh: 所以，例如，Marco，我们在办公室，我说，这份报告进展如何？

segments.en: Is it, you know, were the numbers good?
And I can say, yeah, the numbers seemed all right, but we'll just wait and see.
segments.zh: 我可以说，是的，数字似乎还不错，但我们会拭目以待。

segments.en: Perhaps we don't have all the numbers yet, so we have to wait to get the rest of them.
segments.zh: 也许我们还没有所有的数字，所以我们必须等待得到剩下的数字。

segments.en: That's right.
So you're just basically saying I don't know what will happen in the future.
segments.zh: 所以你只是说我不知道未来会发生什么。

segments.en: Let's just hope that it will be good and let's see what happens.
segments.zh: 让我们只希望它会很好，让我们看看会发生什么。

segments.en: Let's just wait and see.
Let's just wait and see.
All right.

segments.zh: 让我们回去最后一次听我们的对话。

segments.en: And guy last night at a networking party.

segments.zh: 好的，这是我们闲聊系列的另一部分。

segments.en: As you see, very useful and quick little phrases so you can have a very brief conversation with maybe someone you haven't seen or a little chit chat at the office.
segments.zh: 正如您所看到的，非常有用和快速的小短语，因此您可以与可能没有见过的人进行非常简短的交谈，或者在办公室进行一些闲聊。

segments.en: That's right and these are things that if you remember them, you memorize them, you can use in almost any conversation.
segments.zh: 没错，如果你记住它们，你记住它们，你几乎可以在任何对话中使用这些东西。

segments.en: Also I'm sorry to hear that or good for you.
segments.zh: 还有 I'm sorry to hear that 或者 good for you。

segments.zh: 这些是非常非常灵活的短语。

segments.zh: 我很遗憾听到这个消息。
